newsitem.title: TUNISIA: Algeria-Italy gas pipeline to be doubled by January.
newsitem.headline: Algeria-Italy gas pipeline to be doubled by January.

text.p: A natural gas pipeline built to twin one already running from Algeria to Italy will come onstream by January 1997, allowing a flow rate of a total 24 billion cubic metres a year from 12 billion now, an Italian gas company official said on Wednesday.

"Works will be finished by the end of December, and the total maximum volume of 24 billion cubic metres a year through the pipeline will be reached by January," Angelo Ferrari, manager of the gas infrastructure planning department of SNAM SpA, an Italian ENI SpA subsidiary, told Reuters in Tunis.
SNAM in 1983 started operating the Trans-Mediterranean pipeline also called TRANSMED, which runs for 2,500 km (1,550 mile) from the gas fields of Hassi R'Mel in Algeria to the Po Valley in Italy.
TRANSMED, which was designed to transport 12 billion cubic metres, passes through Tunisia and the Sicilian channel in the Mediterranean.
The work to double the gas flow, which started in 1992, was scheduled to be completed by 1995, but some additional improvements in the pumping stations had been necessary, energy sources said.

A Trans-Maghreb pipeline, linking Algeria and Spain through Morocco, came onstream earlier this month with an initial capacity estimated at eight billion cubic metres a year, with a final configuration of 18 billion.
Ferrari was attending a seminar in Tunis on the role of direct foreign investment in the gas industry.
